shardDecision: The slice is 11 files and 237 changed lines and its How to shard section names one shard of code-reviewer-open on opus. I dispatched that one child over the whole slice and held the four parts a child cannot see — the requirement sweep, the boundary sweep, blast radius and the role transition — plus the confirmation of both earlier blockers, which I checked against their witnesses in the code myself rather than taking the child's word. I kept 9 of the child's 10 claims after checking each against the file it names, restated one (S1-8) whose witness does not describe this run, and added four findings of my own that span files no single shard held: the contracts' stale row count, the banner drawn about a country whose provider call is still in flight, Validation Rule 4 against the stricter filter now shipped, and the carry-forward of pass 1's still-open notes.

sweep5.detail: Walked the bundle section by section. §Functional Requirements: all 25 REQ ids have a named artefact (grep -rl 'REQ-02-0NN' apps packages e2e, filtered to the holiday files — every id resolves; REQ-02-022's artefact is the written/skipped/discarded triple in holiday-sourcing.service.ts:216-226 rather than a comment carrying the id). §Routes: 5 new routes exist (holiday-sourcing.controller.ts:26,32 and holiday-sourcing-settings.controller.ts:24,29 under @Controller('api/organizations/:orgId') and '.../settings/holiday-sourcing'), and the list route's two additions exist (holidays.service.ts:147 sourcing block, :422 source field). §Error Messages: all 9 exports exist in packages/validation/src/holiday-sourcing.ts:24-46 and are pinned verbatim at holiday-sourcing.test.ts:106-124. §Data Model: HolidayImport, OrganizationHolidaySourcing and Holiday.source/externalKey/importedAt all present in the migration and schema.prisma. §Validation Rules: 1-3 server-side at holiday-sourcing.service.ts:152,163 and holiday-sourcing-settings.service.ts:67; 4-7 in acceptProviderEntries and buildSourcedCountrySet. §Required data-testid: all 19 rows resolve to a data-testid in the holidays screen (see sweep9). §External Contracts / the double: every behaviour of the 'what the double must reproduce' table has a branch in fake-holiday.provider.ts:233-254. Test ids: all 22 of the bundle's TC ids exist and at the level the bundle puts them (2 unit in packages/validation, 16 int in apps/api/test, 4 e2e in e2e/tests). Env: the three HOLIDAY_PROVIDER_* variables are in .env.example:138-144 and read by resolveHolidayProviderConfig. No section contributed nothing.

sweep9.detail: The pairs checked and agreeing: HOLIDAY_SOURCING_MESSAGES ↔ §Error Messages table (all seven strings, character for character); uncoveredMessage(state) ↔ §UI Description's per-state mapping ↔ Edge case 5a; SourcingState in apps/web/.../types.ts:24 ↔ stateOf in holiday-sourcing.service.ts ↔ the API's three states; the testid roster ↔ the screen (19/19); the roster ↔ the e2e selectors; TC-02-E2E-03 ↔ fake-holiday.provider.ts's VA branch (empty) and IN branch (fail); cases.md TC-02-E2E-02 ↔ the rewritten test; validateSyncYear/validateRefreshFlag/validateIncludeOrgCountry ↔ their server call sites; HolidaySourcingSettings ↔ both call sites in page.tsx (:331, :436 — the two inline casts pass 1 found are gone); resolveCurrencyAtDate ↔ resolveRateAtDate through the one shared newestSnapshotOnOrBefore; byCurrency presence ↔ REQ-02-018; the three env vars ↔ resolveHolidayProviderConfig ↔ .env.example; HolidayImport.holidayCount ↔ written+skipped ↔ REQ-02-021; migration.sql ↔ schema.prisma; summary.year ↔ the HolidaySummary year prop (now guarded); the HolidayProvider port ↔ both drivers and the test stub; PL_DAYS/US_DAYS in the e2e ↔ polandShape/unitedStatesShape. Blast radius: the only shared code touched is packages/validation/src/reports.ts, where resolveRateAtDate was refactored onto newestSnapshotOnOrBefore with the same selection rule and no test weakened (reports.test.ts only gains cases), and HolidayRow gained a required `source` which every existing consumer receives from the one serializer that builds it. Role transition: the new gates all run can(normalizeRole(role), …) (holiday-sourcing.service.ts:445, holiday-sourcing-settings.service.ts:8), so both the stored values and the target set are handled; no new authorization code was added to the shipped holiday gates, so CR-04 does not fire (the asymmetry pass 1 raised as S1-N1 is still open, as a note).

witness.detail: e2e/tests/holidays.spec.ts:527-543. `page.waitForResponse` is armed before the click and matches only a POST to /holidays/sync whose `postDataJSON().refresh === true`, so a click that sends nothing hangs it to the test timeout; then `expect(status).toBeVisible()` and `toContainText(syncing)` are asserted before `toHaveCount(0)`, the shape TC-02-E2E-01 uses at :445-448. `holiday-sourcing-status` is rendered only while `syncing` (HolidaySourcingPanel.tsx:69), which runSync sets synchronously before its fetch (page.tsx:346), so the assertion observes the click's own effect rather than a race. The implementer records having verified it by breaking the code — with `onRefresh` a no-op the case fails at the visibility assertion (stages/implement.attempt-4.md, 'Commands run'), which is the check this finding asked for.

findings.rule: an abandoned read leaves the summary claiming it is still loading
findings.claim: `loadSummary` sets `summaryLoading` true and returns on an abort without ever clearing it, and the auto-sync effect aborts that signal at the moment its own success flips `needsSync` false — so a successful automatic sync can leave the summary block on its preloader until the year tab moves. `runSync` guards exactly this with a run counter in `finally`; the two reads it drives do not.

witness.detail: An admin opens Settings › Holidays on a year whose countries are all unsourced. The effect at page.tsx:404-411 issues runSync with `controller.signal` and returns `() => controller.abort()`. runSync awaits `Promise.all([load(signal), loadSummary(signal)])` (:371). `load` resolves first and calls setSourcing with a block in which every country is now `sourced` (:211), so `needsSync` (:397-400) flips to false; React commits that render and runs the previous effect's cleanup, which aborts the signal `loadSummary` is still waiting on. In loadSummary, `setSummaryLoading(true)` ran at :283, the fetch rejects with AbortError, the catch at :302 returns before `setSummaryLoading(false)` at :306, and the trailing `if (signal?.aborted) return` guards it too. Nothing re-runs loadSummary for the same year — the read effect's deps are `load`/`loadSummary`, whose identities depend only on orgId/year/country — so HolidaySummary keeps rendering the Preloader branch (HolidaySummary.tsx:46) with the figures sitting on the server. I verified each line and the effect ordering rather than taking the shard's word. Kept as a note, not raised to a blocker, for two reasons: the window is the few milliseconds between `load`'s commit and the summary response, and the paths that reach it — TC-02-E2E-01 and TC-02-E2E-04, both of which sync a set that ends fully `sourced` — are recorded green in stages/implement.attempt-4.md ('20 passed'), so the race does not reproduce in the reference environment; and CR-18's 'class of call sites' is a reading of one unhandled path rather than a mechanism plainly missing at several. A slower summary read than list read is what makes it fire, which is a loaded database.

findings.suggestedFix: clear `summaryLoading` (and `loading`) in a `finally` guarded by a run counter, the way runSync guards `setSyncing` at page.tsx:381 — its own comment states the rule: 'a run that was abandoned must not leave one up forever'

findings.rule: the year guard is applied to the summary and not to the warning beside it
findings.claim: This pass added `summary.year !== year` to HolidaySummary so the block never labels one year's figures with another year's heading, and `needsSync` already asks `sourcing.year === year` — but `uncovered` and `hasUnsourced` read `sourcing` with no such check, so after a year-tab change the warning keeps naming the previous year's uncovered countries for the whole of the new year's list read.

witness.detail: A member resolves to IN, which the provider refuses. Under the current year the banner carries `holiday-sourcing-uncovered-IN` with `countryNotCovered`. The admin clicks the tab for year+1, for which IN was recorded `empty` by an earlier sync: `load(signal)` for the new year is in flight and `sourcing` still holds the old year's block, so page.tsx:584-585 keeps drawing the IN line with `countryNotCovered` under a year whose state is `empty` — the very sentence Edge case 5a says that state must never carry. The summary beside it now correctly waits (HolidaySummary.tsx:46), which is what makes the two disagree on screen at the same instant. `isEmpty` at :583 reads the same stale `hasUnsourced`.

findings.suggestedFix: derive both from `sourcing?.year === year ? sourcing.countries : []`, the question needsSync already asks at :399

findings.rule: contracts §Validation Rules row 4 vs the filter that now ships
findings.claim: The code now discards a provider date that names a day its month does not have; the document's Rule 4 still states the constraint as the format and the year only, so the two disagree about what a conforming entry is and the document is the weaker statement.

witness.detail: contracts.md:195 — '| 4 | A provider entry's `date` | `YYYY-MM-DD` and inside the requested year | discarded silently, counted | yes |'. Against it, packages/validation/src/holiday-sourcing.ts:190-196 adds isRealCalendarDay, which round-trips the value through a UTC Date and requires the same string back, and :239 discards when it fails; holiday-sourcing.test.ts:210-219 pins that `2026-02-31` is discarded. Under the document as written that entry passes Rule 4 and the §Decision table's first row then creates a Holiday for it. The code's reading is the better one — asUtcDate (holiday-sourcing.service.ts:470) rolls `2026-02-31` to 3 March, so the document's reading stores a paid day the provider never offered — which is why this is addressed to the document rather than to the code, and why it is a note: an implementation satisfying the document literally exists, it is just the wrong one.

findings.suggestedFix: state Rule 4 as '`YYYY-MM-DD`, a day that exists, and inside the requested year'

The table above it (:139-147) marks `—` on syncFailedSome, countryNotCovered, countryNoHolidays, syncing and summaryUnavailable: five. packages/validation/src/holiday-sourcing.ts:20 repeats 'The four rows the table marks `—`', and packages/validation/src/holiday-sourcing.test.ts:105 names its suite '§Error Messages — the six rows, verbatim' while asserting seven at :106-124. findings.rule: the document is silent where the code now decides
findings.claim: Keying `byCurrency` on financial settings rather than on the accumulated map is the better reading and closes pass 1's S1-N2, but it produces a body shape the bundle names nowhere — a member who holds settings and whom no holiday reached now carries `byCurrency: []` — and that rule now lives only in the code and in an integration test with no case id.

witness.detail: REQ-02-018 ('IF a member has no financial settings, THEN THE SYSTEM SHALL omit their amounts entirely') and contracts.md:125 ('It is **absent** — not empty, not null — on a member with no financial settings') both speak only of the member without settings, so neither forbids the empty list; holiday-summary.service.ts:270 now sends it, pinned by apps/api/test/holiday-sourcing.spec.ts:762-766 under no numbered case. The condition is exactly 'has settings': a snapshot is only ever written in the same transaction that upserts the live row (vacation.service.ts:329-339), which I checked, so `history.length > 0 && live === null` is unreachable. Under Edge case 23 — an empty sourced set — every member with settings now carries `byCurrency: []` where they previously carried no key, which is a response-shape change no document records.

findings.suggestedFix: add the row beside Edge case 16 — 'A member with settings whom no holiday reached: `byCurrency` present and empty' — and give the new integration case an id

findings.rule: a bound proportional to the call bound also has to cover the writes in the same request
findings.claim: The tightened margin is right in intent — a fixed +5000ms passed against a service that ignored the configured bound — but `callBoundMs * 4` is 1200ms measured around the whole HTTP request, which also signs in, resolves the country set, writes 14 Polish holidays one create at a time and records two imports. Roughly three quarters of the budget belongs to work the bound says nothing about, so a loaded database and a timing regression now fail the same way.

witness.detail: apps/api/test/holiday-sourcing.spec.ts:806 sets provider.callBoundMs = 300; :814 asserts elapsed < callBoundMs * 4 over `sync(...)`, which performs the PL import (14 rows through writeEntries' per-date existence check) and the IN abandonment in one request. The previous assertion was callBoundMs + 5000.

findings.suggestedFix: time the mechanism rather than the request — a sync whose only country is `neverAnswers` has no writes to pay for, and `callBoundMs * 4` over that is a bound on the deadline itself

findings.rule: the comment names a different mechanism from the one the line performs
findings.claim: The comment says 'Read the body to completion before abandoning it'; the line cancels the body, which is the correct way to release the socket and is not what the sentence describes. The behaviour is right — this closes pass 1's S2-N3 — and only the comment is wrong, on the line a reader consults before changing it.

witness.detail: apps/api/src/holidays/provider/nager-holiday.provider.ts:42-45 — the comment above `await response.body?.cancel().catch(() => undefined);`. Optional chaining short-circuits the whole call chain when `response.body` is null, so the null case is safe, the `.catch` swallows a cancel racing the abort, and the throw still reaches REQ-02-009's unsourced path. The non-array branch below needs no equivalent because `response.json()` has already drained the body.

findings.suggestedFix: 'Release the body before abandoning the response' — a cancel is a release, not a read

findings.rule: a tool read without its run id answers about a different run
findings.claim: The shard reported that `review-slice.mjs` printed a 13-file slice at base 384d8c6 against the 11 files at base 22ac051 the prompt named, and cleared the difference by diffing the two extra files. I restate it: run with no run id the script does not describe this run at all — it prints 'pass 1' for a different run directory — so the two outputs were never about the same change, and the run's own accounting is unaffected.

witness.detail: `node scripts/review-slice.mjs 2026-09-07T10-33-36_time-off-02-holiday-sourcing --shape lead-open` prints '# Review slice — pass 2 / # 22ac051..98177a4 — what review 1 judged / the whole change is 31 files; this slice is 11'. `node scripts/review-slice.mjs` with no arguments prints '# Review slice — pass 1 / # 384d8c6..98177a4 — the run base — this is the first pass / the whole change is 13 files; this slice is 13' — a different run base and a different scope. The shard's own check still holds and is worth keeping: `git diff 22ac051..HEAD -- apps/api/src/holidays/provider/holiday-provider.ts apps/api/test/stub-holiday.provider.ts` is empty, so nothing outside the 11 moved since the last judgement.

findings.suggestedFix: none for this run; if the script can tell that it was run inside a run directory, defaulting to that run would stop the next reader reviewing a slice from somewhere else

findings.rule: carry-forward — pass 1 notes left open on purpose
findings.claim: Nine of pass 1's fifteen notes were closed by this attempt and I confirmed each against the code. Six remain open and none of them is a blocker; they are listed here so a person reads them in one place, with their witnesses in stages/review.attempt-1.json.

witness.detail: Closed and verified: S3-6 (impossible dates discarded, holiday-sourcing.ts:190/239), S1-N2 (byCurrency on settings, holiday-summary.service.ts:270 — see L5), S2-N3 (body cancelled, nager-holiday.provider.ts:42 — see L7), S2-N1 (margin now callBoundMs * 4 — see L6), S3-4 (global row keyed on the API's own value, HolidaySummary.tsx:210; the roster still names no id for it and no test selects it), S3-5 (a member with no country renders '—', HolidaySummary.tsx:103), S3-8 (summary year guard, HolidaySummary.tsx:47), S3-3 (autoSynced.current.delete(year) on abort and on a non-200, page.tsx:361 and :376 — I checked the effect cannot loop: a non-200 changes no dependency, so nothing re-issues), S3-7 (HolidaySourcingSettings used at both call sites, page.tsx:331 and :436). Still open: S1-N1 (the shipped holiday gates do not run normalizeRole while the new ones do — holidays.service.ts:269,278; no new authorization code was added there, so CR-04 does not fire), S1-N3 (holiday rows and the import record are written in two statements with no transaction, holiday-sourcing.service.ts:207/218), S1-N4 (`holidayCount` names the offered count in the sourcing block and a row count in the summary, and no sentence defines the first), S2-N2 (nothing at any level exercises NagerHolidayProvider or resolveHolidayProviderConfig — the only driver a deployed environment selects), S3-9 (with a country filter applied and any country unsourced, the list area renders neither empty state — page.tsx:583, `isEmpty = noHolidays && !hasUnsourced`, with `isCountryFiltered` only reached through isEmpty), and pass 1's L1 (no web file re-runs Validation Rules 1 to 3 before spending a request, which the contracts say the client does; the server half is present and correct, so CR-08 does not fire).

findings.suggestedFix: none required to proceed; S2-N2 and pass 1's L1 are the two a person should rule on, because one leaves the production driver unrun and the other leaves a sentence in the contracts that nothing implements
